note: Scored by Lane B (Paridhi Singh), Nov 14, 2026. This ranking is the team's judgement, not NASA's. Fire-safety +3 goes to any sub-area mentioning 'fire', plus all three Saffire experiments (PSI-98, PSI-99, PSI-100) as one NASA project — a team call, not NASA's.

experiments.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II)
experiments.test_count_source: our PSI-25 table, counted by code
experiments.summary: Burns solid samples such as fabric, plastic rods and films in a space station wind tunnel, at flows up to 40 cm/s and oxygen below 21%, to study ignition, spread and extinction for fire-safety models.

experiments.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS)
experiments.test_count_source: our PSI-26 CSV: 122 table lines, of which 1 is a 'SOOT Cleaning' line and 121 are tests (PSI page shows 123)
experiments.summary: Burned SIBAL fabric, PMMA spheres and other samples on the space station at flows up to 40 cm/s to link NASA's standard flammability test to real microgravity burning, and tested nitrogen as an extinguisher.

experiments.title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II (SAFFIRE-II)
experiments.test_count_source: our PSI-99 table, counted by code (one sample row split in two)
experiments.summary: Second Cygnus fire experiment: burned nine 5 cm by 29 cm samples (SIBAL, silicone and PMMA types, PMMA with Nomex) to measure fire growth and flammability limits in low gravity.

experiments.title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-III (SAFFIRE-III)
experiments.test_count_source: our PSI-100 table, counted by code
experiments.summary: Third Cygnus fire experiment: burned SIBAL fabric at 30 cm/s, once with concurrent and once with opposed flow, to measure fire growth and flammability limits.

experiments.title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment-I (SAFFIRE-I)
experiments.test_count_source: our PSI-98 table, counted by code
experiments.summary: Burned a large SIBAL fabric sample on a Cygnus spacecraft at 20 cm/s to see how fast a big fire grows in low gravity and how its flammability limit compares to NASA's normal-gravity test.
